Dear all,

I am a bit new to Latent Variable Analysis and lavaan. One practical question is how can I set my model but using the "effect coding" for scaling in lavaan?
A conceptual question. It is said that the Latent approach account for the "measurement error" in the measures, but how that happens from an algorithmic or mathematical perspective?

Thank you!
Michael.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: effect coding and "measurement error accounted for"
parts: how can I set my model but using the "effect coding" for scaling in lavaan?

By using labels for model parameters and setting nonlinear parameter constraints.  For example, in a 3-indicator factor:

f =~ L1*x1 + L2*x2 + L3*x3
x1 ~ T1*1
x2 ~ T2*1
x3 ~ T3*1
## parameter constraints
L3 == 3 - L1 - L2
T3 == 0 - T1 - T2
A conceptual question. It is said that the Latent approach account for the "measurement error" in the measures, but how that happens from an algorithmic or mathematical perspective?

The short answer is that measurement error is explicitly represented as parameters in the model.  Point estimates of factor loadings and residual (measurement error) variances are chosen that best reproduce the observed covariance matrix.  There are many SEM textbooks available that describe the details of how measurement-model parameters are identified and estimated, using any number of algorithms (e.g., maximum likelihood).  This sort of general SEM question is better posted on the SEMNET forum:

http://www2.gsu.edu/~mkteer/semnet.html

Terry
